_about: An extraction stage: one request to the model that reads the paper and fills these columns for every row. A pack can have several (one file each, run in parallel). Every field is explained in README.md ('Stages'). This EXAMPLE reads simple conditions and one result: rename it and replace the parameters with your own.
name: example_measurements
label: Measurements (example)
description: Conditions and results of each experiment (the template's example stage).
system_prompt: Extract experimental conditions and results from a scientific paper. Report only what the paper states.
_about_trigger: When the stage runs: always, or only for papers that need it -- set_types (e.g. ['Time Series']), keywords in the paper text, set_patterns (regexes on set labels).
_about_per: 'sample': a value can belong to one row; 'set': values are per set (or '' = the whole paper).
intro: For every experiment set (and sample) in the structure plan below, extract the values the paper reports. A value that holds for every set goes in ONE row with `set` ''; a value that differs between sets goes in each set's row; one that differs between the samples of a set goes in each sample's row.
_about_parameters: One entry per column this stage fills: column (from columns.json, or a new one), unit (the column's unit; values are converted into it), description (the model reads it: say exactly what belongs there), kind 'text' for words instead of numbers, choices (a fixed list of allowed words), integer (a count), uncertainties (also <column>_err_plus / _err_minus).

parameters.description: the temperature the experiment ran at.
the pressure the experiment ran at (atmospheric = 1 bar only when the paper says ambient or atmospheric pressure).
the pH of the solution at the start of the experiment.
the material or substance studied, as the paper names it.
how the result was measured (instrument or technique), at most 8 words.
the yield of the product, in %.

_about_rules: Extra instructions for the model, one sentence each, about anything the descriptions don't cover.
rules: A value read from the setup (e.g. 'sealed glass ampoule' for a sealed vessel) is b 'derived': quote the setup.
_about_open_ended: true: the model also lists values that have no column (`other`), offered in the review as new variables; open_ended_hint says what to look for and what to leave out.
open_ended_hint: e.g. other conditions of the experiment (stirring, light, atmosphere) and other measured results. Not the values of the parameters above.
